## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `SetupGuide`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `twitter-setup-guide`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **SetupGuide**.

## Step 2: Create a Twitter developer project

1. <!-- manual: Open the [Twitter Developer Portal](https://developer.twitter.com/en/portal/dashboard). -->
2. Select **Projects & Apps** tab and select an existing project or create a new one.

## Step 3: Set up user authentication

1. In your project or app settings, select **Set up** to configure user authentication.
2. <!-- manual: Complete the user authentication setup by filling in the required fields (app permissions, callback URI, website URL). -->

## Step 4: Get an access token (OAuth 2.0 PKCE flow)

1. <!-- manual: Construct the authorization URL: Replace ‹YOUR_CLIENT_ID›, ‹YOUR_REDIRECT_URI›, and ‹YOUR_CODE_CHALLENGE› with your values. Adjust the scope parameter as needed. :::note Two code challenge methods are available: S256 (SHA256 hash of the code verifier, recommended) and plain (the verifier string itself). ::: -->
2. <!-- manual: Open the URL in a browser and authorize the app when prompted. -->
3. After authorization, you are redirected to your callback URI with an authorization `code` in the URL. Copy the code. :::warning The authorization code expires quickly — use it immediately. :::.
4. <!-- manual: Exchange the code for tokens: -->
5. <!-- manual: Copy the access_token from the response. :::note By default, access tokens obtained through this flow are valid for two hours. To obtain a long-lived token, add offline.access to your scopes — see the [Twitter documentation](https://developer.x.com/en/docs/authentication/oauth-2-0/user-access-token) for details. ::: -->
